channel.title: Crypto Record
channel.description: Crypto Record reports news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation and network upgrades across the crypto market.

item.title: What Happens When a Bridge Token Callback Fails
item.description: A callback can fail after a bridge transfer moves, leaving the destination action incomplete; recovery depends on message state and retry rules.

item.title: How BSC Swap Routes Work, and Which Ones Fail Less
item.description: A BSC swap route is more reliable when its pools, quote and execution limits agree; compare liquidity, hop count and minimum output before signing.

item.title: Three Checks Before You Trust a BSC Token Chart
item.description: A BSC token chart reflects trades in a specific liquidity pool; check the token address, pool depth and transaction history before treating its price as meaningful.

item.title: Three Signals That Show a Bridge Deposit Is Complete
item.description: A bridge deposit is complete only when the destination transaction succeeds and settles; source confirmation and a pending relay are earlier stages, not proof of delivery.

item.title: Why Polygon bridge transfers take different amounts of time
item.description: Polygon bridge time depends on direction: deposits wait for Ethereum confirmation and Polygon processing, while withdrawals add a validator checkpoint and an Ethereum claim.

item.title: Five Checks for Omnichain Routes as Networks Change
item.description: Routing depends on contracts, verifiers and execution rules lining up across chains; five checks help keep the path valid when networks or settings change.

item.title: Why a Cross-Chain Transfer Is Stuck and When to Retry
item.description: A cross-chain transfer can be sent on one chain and still await proof or execution on another; check its stage before retrying to avoid a duplicate action.

item.title: The Cost of Moving Rebasing Tokens Across Chains
item.description: Moving a rebasing token costs more than one bridge quote: compare source and destination gas, bridge charges, and any wrapping or swap needed to preserve rewards.

item.title: When Does Splitting a Cross-Chain Swap Pay?
item.description: Splitting a large cross-chain swap can reduce price impact, but extra routes add fees, timing risk and failure points that can erase the gain quickly.

item.title: Bridged XMR Needs a Treasury Fund’s Payment Route
item.description: Bridged XMR must become an eligible payment asset before it can buy Treasury fund shares; ZeroFi currently routes zXMR to Sepolia, so real purchases stop there.

item.title: How Bridged XMR Becomes EVM Lending Collateral
item.description: Bridged XMR can serve as EVM lending collateral only when its wrapper, oracle, liquidity and liquidation route work together, each with risks to manage.

item.title: How to Confirm zXMR Arrived on Sepolia
item.description: Confirm zXMR on Sepolia by checking the bridge transaction, matching the token contract, and verifying the received balance in your wallet or explorer.

item.title: How Arbitrage Aligns TRON Swap Pool Prices
item.description: TRON swap pool prices shift as trades change token reserves; arbitrageurs trade price gaps until fees, slippage and execution costs erase the profit.

item.title: How to swap an airdropped TRC-20 token for USDT
item.description: A TRC-20 airdrop becomes USDT only through a supported market: verify the token contract, compare the quote, fund TRON fees, then confirm the swap.

item.title: How Pool Fee Rebates Change the Cost of a TRON Swap
item.description: A pool fee rebate returns part of a swap charge under stated rules; compare the net amount with route quality, TRON network resources and any claim cost before trading.

item.title: What TRON Swap Energy Pays For—and How You Cover It
item.description: TRON swap Energy pays for smart-contract execution. Staking, delegation, TRX burns and contract settings determine who covers a swap’s resource cost.

item.title: A Cross-Chain Transfer Is Stuck. Which Step Failed?
item.description: A cross-chain transfer can pause at confirmation, routing, liquidity or destination execution; check each stage in order before retrying or sending funds again.

item.title: Why a Swap Can Stay Pending: Tick Arrays Explained
item.description: Tick arrays supply ranges a concentrated-liquidity swap can cross; a bad sequence can fail execution, while network confirmation determines how long it stays pending.

item.title: Why a Native Bridge Withdrawal Can Take Days
item.description: Native bridge withdrawals wait for a chain’s exit proof and security window to clear; the delay depends on the rollup design, then a final claim releases funds.

item.title: How to Find Wallets Buying Near Local Lows
item.description: Finding wallets that buy near local lows means matching swap records to price turns, then checking whether those addresses held or quickly sold what they acquired.
